newsitem.title: FRANCE: Golf-Woosnam rattled says rival Montgomerie.
newsitem.headline: Golf-Woosnam rattled says rival Montgomerie.

text.p: Colin Montgomerie senses that Ian Woosnam is uneasy about their unfolding battle for this year's European Order of Merit crown.
Woosnam's suggestion at the Lancome Trophy on Friday that Montgomerie has benefited from early start times in recent tournaments was clear evidence to the Scot that his Welsh rival is rattled.
"He is worried now. It's great," the Scot said with a sly smile. "I'm delighted he is asking those questions."
"He says he is fed up, I'm delighted. He says I'm posting a good score before he plays. Fine -- is there a problem with that?" Montgomerie asked mischievously.
He added, seriously: "They are never going to play us together, for television and for obvious reasons. Probably next week it will go the other way."
If fact, Montgomerie said, he'd rather play late the first day and early the second rather than the other way around.
"If I had a choice, which I don't, that's what I'd like. I did not ask. I take the draw as it comes."
Montgomerie, chasing a record-equalling fourth successive Order of Merit title, leads Woosnam by 60,000 pounds ($93,000) following his impressive win at the European Masters last week.
"There's always somebody. Last year it was Sam Torrance, this year it's Woosie. I'm tired mentally, but this keeps me going," Montgomerie said.
Woosnam is fighting a neck and back problem diagnosed as spondylosis, a degeneration of two vertebrae in his spine.
He has been having treatment here, but back trouble is nothing new. "I have always played with a bad back. It means I don't practise much, just a few shots before I go out," he said.
Woosnam shared the lead with Jesper Parnevik of Sweden heading into Saturday's third round, with Montgomerie a shot behind.
The Welshman was not letting his physical problems distract him from his efforts to overhaul his rival. "Someone has to stop him. I am still playing well and I am determined," Woosnam said.

With 108,330 pounds ($168,000) going to the winner and three more qualifying events before the season-ending Volvo Masters, the battle could go down to the final putt of the season -- just like last year when Montgomerie beat Torrance with a three-footer on the last green at Valderrama.
